name: Medial meniscus posterior root
description: Attachment of the medial posterior horn to the posterior intercondylar tibia, behind the medial eminence and just in front of the PCL. Low signal, often striated; coronal fluid-sensitive images show it best.

normal_values.attachment_center: about 9.6 mm posterior and 0.7 mm lateral to the medial tibial eminence apex (cadaver)
normal_values.distance_to_pcl_attachment: about 8 mm in cadavers but about 3 mm on 7 T MRI; a root close to the PCL is normal

variants_pitfalls: Striation alone is not a tear. A full-height cleft or a missing root is a complete tear; a partial-height cleft is a partial tear, not striation.

Root tear = radial tear or avulsion within about 9–10 mm of the attachment: a vertical cleft or truncation on coronal T2, a ghost meniscus on sagittal, a radial cleft on axial. Partial tears rarely give a ghost sign.

Extrusion over 3 mm is the main secondary sign (root tear in 42% vs 3%). A medial femoral condyle insufficiency fracture should send you to the root (medial root or posterior horn radial tears in 71% of one series).
A ghost meniscus also follows a complete posterior horn radial tear, meniscectomy or root repair; check the history.
